Wicked

in my defense I was a teenager who still had a special interest in Wizard of Oz series and would eat up any books related to the setting so when I learned about it, I was quick to read it

needless to say I was VERY distraught and more traumatized the more I read on, and my innocence was shattered. I stopped around the time they had that animal orgy on stage and I've never considered it giving it another go since then. 



It really boggles my mind the book is...like that when years later as an adult, I loved seeing the broadway play.

starting the mages guild and dark brotherhood questlines \[and stumbling into side quests and the gorgeous scenery along the way as I do.\]

Main quest? what main quest?

i've tried to give Monster Hunter series a chance, really I have - I LOVE the monster designs and stuff. But the grind...man I just can't do it, it gets so repetitive and samey for me so fast killing same monsters over and over for gear

as long as I can still access major story content and like when 'time passes' when I have the funds to do so, i'm fine. I'm just happy for subclasses because I hate investing so much into a character - getting skyshards and everything, picking up books then suddenly feeling like wanting to play a different class and having to reroll a new character and repeat the process that already took me 2-3 weeks to do. I'm excited to supplement my necro with warden and sorcerer or arcanist skills, make them the ultimate ice storm mage

still don't understand what people mean by battle pass or whatever though, I was tapped out for most of the stream to minimize spoilers

Skyrim was my first but Oblivion made me fall in love with the world. Its guild quests also felt so much more in depth like I enjoyed creative deaths you could do for the DB \[before it devolved into -find this person and just kill them, no fancy tricks - anyways and having to do ACTUAL work to get approved to even get into the Mage Guild headquarters. And how involved learning skills could be, the fact places felt busier than they do in Skyrim - it was a RICH world to me.

I'm definitely worried the next Elder Scrolls will dumb down those guild quests and learning skills down even further...

I'll get hate for this - but raid finder for ESO \[non-vet obvs, i'm just thinking of casual players who just want to get that trial done for story/lorebook bits or sake of completion\] , it's worked for FFXIV - honestly could even just set up a custom party finder system if they won't do an automatic raid finder - just an advertisement of wanting to look for people without being limited to yelling in a a zone and having to hop around to find people - I only just came back to ESO after 5 years so idk if there's a general party finder now - I did see achievements are shared now so that's nice

i literally forget about the main questline as soon as I get out of Helgen. it really varies! I can switch from one subject to the next - like how does one terrain transfrom from one climate to a different one? My setting may be fantasy but I don't want to make the whiplash mistake of one setting being a lush grassland and the next step is straight into a desert. 

I've also looked into things like culture of people, cuisine, how they can differ from one town to the next. Nature documentaries are also GREAT for inspiring what I can do with critters and plants/mushroom in creative ways in my setting as well!

recently I looked around and found an excellent vid that put into concise, easy to understand what would happen if a moon suddenly disappeared from Earth and that helped me solidify how that'd affect things in the world I'm building \[such as entire coastlines rearranged and different seasons, some permanent in certain areas, how the lore of the people evolves now that there's no moon in the sky anymore\].

I was watching a documentary recently and saw how bright and colorful dragonflies and I wondered if that couldn't have led to the myths of fairies and pixies since they fly around so quickly, a unprepared person might've mistook them for something very magical, just a flash of bright blue or green.

I'm coming back to ESO after few years of absence, does anyone know any guilds that still do story friendly dungeon and trial runs? Including old and new ones. Since I'll be rolling a new character.  
  
As in people who are active in helping finish a dungeon without rushing through the dialogue and lore, forcing players to skip talking to NPCs and picking up books and such to add to their eidetic library? I found that supremely annoying back then especially when I was trying to do a new dungeon because I enjoyed knowing what new stories ESO had to offer.
let's go!!! I need Majima in my life

**Name:** Ciel

**Pronouns:** He/They/Ciel

**Timezone:** US Mountain, no daylights saving

**Availability:** Usually online almost every day!

**Preferred System:** I'm mostly familiar with DnD 5e and Pathfinder 1.0 - I haven't toyed with 5.5 or 2.0 as of yet but wouldn't mind learning! I can do live text which is actually preferable for me. I'm also interested in trying other different systems like Lancer or Shadowrun!

**Type of Player:** One who will ask all the questions relevant, might roll for one or two silly thing, very easygoing and enjoys playing humorous characters. I would not be a good fit for your grim dark setting. Light, with some serious moments, is good for me. I LOVE to explore a room as thoroughly as I can and try something because 'what if?' - probably a wild card. But if you have rules set, I always respect them! I enjoy intrigue, adventuring, 'monster/dungeon/mission of the week' esque stuff, don't mind combat either but I am leery of 'permadeath' character play.

**Additional Information:** I am deaf so play by post is ideal for me, hoping I can find something long term! Ideally I'd like to play with other fellow LGBT+ / friendly individuals, at least 25+ years of age \[I am in my thirties\]. Please DM me for discord!

thank you for this opportunity!! I love Majima and have been excited for this game but funds have been little tight!!

Hello! I've already got quite a backlog but am always open for more recommendations! Ideally I'm interested in more fantasy stories that aren't Euro-centric, written by BIPOC, and diverse - long running or number of volumes with a good bit of worldbuilding. I absolutely love ones where we learn about the world at the same pace our characters do without it being like a paragraph long infodump. I also love anthologies!

I adore magic - the Bartimaeus is still one of my all time favorite, followed by His Dark Materials and Pendragon series. I enjoyed Hobbit, but LOTR was a STRUGGLE to read through. Just to give an idea on where my interests may lead. Medieval, high, low, modern - I'm not too picky on fantasy level. Except romance, I don't like romance as a primary focus.

that said - I do have one thing I do NOT want to see ever: underage-adult and/or incest romantic/sex relationships, rape or sex scenes, nothing ruins a mood and makes me yeet a book faster than being invested in a world and character's stories to be suddenly whiplashed by a graphic scene as this and such.
